relations.subject: backup:cbbackupmgr-examine-command
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; applied to the documented behavior boundary between collection-aware (7.0.0+) and collection-unaware backups rather than a feature/object pair
relations.evidence: When examining a range of backups which transition from collection unaware to collection aware (for example after upgrading the target cluster to 7.0.0) examine will stop search upon hitting the first collection aware backup.

relations.subject: server/8.0/backup-restore/cbbackupmgr-examine
relations.evidence: For more information see `COLLECTION AWARE BACKUPS` in [cbbackupmgr-backup](cbbackupmgr-backup.md).

notable_absence.finding: Unlike cbbackupmgr-backup.md and cbbackupmgr-restore.md (this batch), which both carry a full RBAC section naming data_backup/analytics_admin/eventing_admin/fts_admin, this page never states what role is required to run examine at all, despite examine being able to return raw document values, metadata and XATTRs (including hex-dumped) for any key in a backup - arguably the most sensitive read operation of any command in this batch, and the one with the least-stated access control.

cross_component_finding: Examine silently stops scanning a backup range at the first collection-aware backup when searching across a collection-unaware-to-collection-aware transition, rather than erroring: 'examine will stop search upon hitting the first collection aware backup, Examine will print a warning indicating that it stopped searching prematurely.' This mirrors the round's caution against assuming automatic correspondence between two things that look alike - here, two backups in the same repository, one collection-aware and one not, are similar enough to both be 'backups in this repo' but different enough that a single examine invocation cannot search across the boundary without an explicit --start/--end restart.
